subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw change memory search chunking to respect Markdown headings by default, add an opt-in chunking strategy/config, or defer chunking until the broader Memory MVP/entity design is settled?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementation changes persisted index identity and retrieval behavior, and the issue also bundles entity/graph-memory direction that needs product ownership.

options.title: Split and approve a narrow chunking design
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

options.title: Make heading-aware default
options.body: Adopt heading boundaries as the canonical behavior for Markdown memory files, accepting that existing headed files will reindex and retrieve differently.

options.title: Defer to Memory MVP design
options.body: Keep this open but wait for memory write/entity pipeline decisions so chunking, extraction, and wiki synthesis land as one coordinated design.

recommendation.title: Split and approve a narrow chunking design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The immediate decision is the memory-core config/API/default and index identity contract, which recent history points to steipete owning most directly.
